info.description: Transactional email for IAM and the MailOS console. Every /api/v1 operation needs an IAM access token (Bearer, or DPoP for sender-constrained tokens). Console users need a MailOS role (mailos_admin, mailos_template_editor, mailos_template_publisher, mailos_operator, mailos_auditor, mailos_viewer); sensitive operations need a sign-in no older than 5 minutes with a second factor and answer 403 STEP_UP_REQUIRED with an RFC 9470 WWW-Authenticate challenge otherwise.

For service clients only (IAM client-credentials token with aud mailos). Body is IAM's event envelope {id, type, source, data, tenant_uuid, organization_uuid}. The client must be an active server application (IAM's own client is the system application seeded from IAM_SERVICE_CLIENT_ID) whose message_types allow the topic; the tenant is the application's, and an event or token naming another is refused; refusals are 403 and audited as event.refused. 202 {accepted, delivery_id, event_id, duplicate}; a repeated id is a duplicate with no second message. Permission: `events:dispatch`.

get.description: Per purpose (provider, dkim, webhook): keys, state and how many values each seals. Never key material. Permission: `settings:manage`. Needs step-up (a sign-in with a second factor within 5 minutes); otherwise 403 STEP_UP_REQUIRED with an RFC 9470 WWW-Authenticate challenge.

post.description: Retires the active key; the schedule re-encrypts what it sealed and then destroys it. Permission: `settings:manage`. Needs step-up (a sign-in with a second factor within 5 minutes); otherwise 403 STEP_UP_REQUIRED with an RFC 9470 WWW-Authenticate challenge.

get.description: The token's subject, tenant, MailOS roles and the permissions they grant. Permission: `templates:read`.

Never bodies; subject and template data masked (secret variables such as OTP codes). Filters: status (including captured for sandbox applications), type, topic, to, from, until, application_id. Permission: `messages:read`.

post.description: Up to 100 messages; each follows the same rules as a single send. The Idempotency-Key covers the whole batch. Permission: `messages:send`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Retry-safe sends: the first response for the key is stored for IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_TTL per application (per tenant for console users) and replayed with Idempotent-Replayed: true; the same key with another body is 409. 5xx and 429 are not stored.

post.description: Direct (subject/html/text) or templated (template_slug or template_id, optional template_locale, template_vars). The send worker uses the template's published version. A suppressed recipient is stored with status suppressed. For an application's service token (client credentials, aud mailos): the tenant is the application's; the message type (topic or template slug, or raw for written content) must be among its message_types; the sender must be one of its senders on a verified domain (its default sender when none is named); a transactional application cannot send marketing, a broadcast application's mail is marketing; then its per-minute rate and daily quota (429). Sandbox applications' messages are captured, never delivered. Refusals are audited as message.refused with a stable reason. Permission: `messages:send`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Retry-safe sends: the first response for the key is stored for IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_TTL per application (per tenant for console users) and replayed with Idempotent-Replayed: true; the same key with another body is 409. 5xx and 429 are not stored.

post.description: HTTPS only. Optional application_id limits the endpoint to that application's messages; without it, it receives every message of the tenant. Deliveries are signed the Standard Webhooks way (webhook-id, webhook-timestamp, webhook-signature v1 HMAC-SHA256; whsec_ secrets). The signing secret is sealed; a generated one is returned once. Permission: `webhooks:manage`. Needs step-up (403 STEP_UP_REQUIRED with an RFC 9470 challenge).

get.description: The tenant's applications: the projects that send through MailOS, each bound to its IAM OAuth client. Filters: status (active, suspended), kind (server, spa). Permission: `applications:read`.

post.description: Binds an IAM client (registered in IAM by the application's owner; MailOS issues no secret or key) to the tenant. Senders must be on the tenant's verified sending domains. A client is one application across all tenants (409). Audited as application.created. Permission: `applications:manage`. Needs step-up (403 STEP_UP_REQUIRED with an RFC 9470 challenge).

put.description: Every editable field. A system application (seeded from configuration) is refused with 403. Audited with before and after. Permission: `applications:manage`. Needs step-up (403 STEP_UP_REQUIRED with an RFC 9470 challenge).

delete.description: Its client is refused from then on; its messages keep the application id. A system application cannot be deleted. Permission: `applications:manage`. Needs step-up (403 STEP_UP_REQUIRED with an RFC 9470 challenge).

post.description: Body {reason}. Every call of the application is refused at once (audited reason application_suspended). Works on a system application too. Permission: `applications:manage`. Needs step-up (403 STEP_UP_REQUIRED with an RFC 9470 challenge).
Lifts a suspension. Permission: `applications:manage`. Needs step-up (403 STEP_UP_REQUIRED with an RFC 9470 challenge).

get.description: Messages per UTC day and status over ?days (1 to 90, default 30), and today's use of the daily quota (-1 when the counter is unavailable). Permission: `applications:read`.

post.description: For a spa application's browser user only: an IAM user access token issued to the application's public client, aud mailos, scope mailos.send.self, carrying email and email_verified=true. Body {template, locale, variables}: the template must be one the application marks browser_allowed; the recipient is always the token's own verified address; there is no sender, recipient or content field. The Origin header must be one of the application's allowed_origins. Per-user hourly limit (429 user_rate_limited), then the application's rate and quota. Refusals are 403 or 429, audited as message.refused with a stable reason. Permission: `messages:send_self`.
